messages:
maria-support: Customer on SDK 0.23.1 reporting 404s for chat endpoints after we shipped model routing changes. They say `client.chat.create` is undefined and `client.request('chat.create')` returns 404.
ryan-eng: can you paste the minimal repro? which package and import style are they using?
maria-support: code snip from customer:
```json
{
  "name": "test-app",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/inference": "0.23.1"
  }
}
```
and this Node code:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.chat.create({ modelName: 'redwood-alpha', input: 'hello' });
```
they say same call via curl to /v1/chat/create returns 200. SDK call errors: `TypeError: client.chat.create is not a function` then if they try `client.request('chat.create', ...)` returns 404 body `route not found`.
leo-devx: sounds like the SDK surface doesn't match server routes. maybe the published SDK codegen used old route names or new route names but not both. did they install from npm or via github tarball?
maria-support: npm `npm i @redwood/inference@0.23.1`. customer confirmed fresh node_modules, cleared cache, still fails. curl against the same API key and host works.
ryan-eng: can you grab the installed package's index (node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.js) and check exported methods? also which TS/JS bundle target?
maria-support: asked customer, they sent `dist/index.js` snippet — there is `chatCreate` camelCase exported function but no `chat.create` namespace. I think our old SDK used nested namespaces, new generated SDK flattened names.
kevin-sre: could be an API surface refactor slipped through without a major version bump. If the server still expects old calls we might have a mismatch in the SDK->server mapping table. Search the repo for `chat.create` mapping in the client shim.
ryan-eng: i pulled the 0.23.1 tag — codegen switched to flat names `chatCreate`, `embedText` in this release. We forgot to publish the compatibility shims that map legacy dotted routes to new names. That explains the undefined `client.chat.create` and the `request('chat.create')` 404 because runtime routing expects `chat.create` to be registered.
leo-devx: workaround for customers: 1) call the flat exports `client.chatCreate({ model: 'redwood-alpha', input: '...' })` or 2) use direct REST `POST /v1/chat/create` as a stopgap. Document both in the support reply.
maria-support: customer tried `client.chatCreate` and it works but their codebase is large and they cannot change quickly. they asked for a patch release to restore the old `client.chat.create` accessor.
ryan-eng: agree we should publish a 0.23.2 patch that reintroduces namespace shims. I'll open a quick PR to the SDK repo to add shims mapping dotted names to the flat functions and bump patch. Can someone sanity-check the shim approach? Keep it lightweight: just attach `client.chat = { create: client.chatCreate }` etc in the constructor.
kevin-sre: also add a small note in the changelog and an opt-in deprecation warning log so customers know to migrate. We should check codegen pipeline to ensure major changes get a major version.
ci-bot: CI pipeline triggered: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/94321 — tests for client-surface passed locally but add a quick integration test calling old dotted names.
ryan-eng: creating PR now, will request review from @leo-devx. ETA < 2 hours for PR, 4 hours for release if tests pass.
maria-support: passing this to customer, gave temporary instructions to call flat methods or curl. Customer extremely grateful for the quick turnaround. They asked to be notified when 0.23.2 is published.
leo-devx: follow-up: add a small migration note in the SDK README and email notify the top 10 app accounts that used `client.chat.create` in the last 30 days.
maria-support: ack, i'll prepare the customer notification draft once release is out.
ryan-eng: keeping thread open until publish. will post release tag + changelog here.
